discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted, with a simple and elegant continuum model, that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that electron-electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realised this regime experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, tunable by a gate voltage in a single device. This theory-experiment pair created the field of moire quantum matter and 'twistronics', which has since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field in moire materials. It turned the twist angle into a new control knob for designing strongly interacting quantum phases, giving a clean, tunable platform for long-standing questions about high-temperature superconductivity and topology. Few recent discoveries in condensed matter physics have been as far-reaching.
